one_line: Kashmiri court poet at Ajmer, composer of the Prithviraja-Vijaya around 1191–93 CE.

appearance.face: oval face, light brown Kashmiri complexion, sharp nose, thoughtful dark eyes behind thin circular metal-framed spectacles, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, default expression calm and observant with a hint of intensity
appearance.hair: straight, black shoulder-length hair parted in the middle and tucked behind ears, mostly hidden under a soft off-white Kashmiri wool cap shaped like a modest rounded pagri with a narrow maroon band at the base
appearance.costume: a long-sleeved knee-length angarkha-style tunic of fine cream-coloured cotton with a subtle woven stripe, side-tied with maroon cloth cords; over it, a sleeveless light wool shawl-vest in muted olive green draped around shoulders and falling to mid-thigh; lower body in loose churidar-style trousers in deep maroon, closely gathered at the ankles; simple brown leather sandals; a narrow dark brown leather belt at the waist with a small cloth pouch; minimal jewellery: a single thin gold ring on the right hand and a small copper tilak box hanging from the belt to hint at devotional practice
appearance.signature: a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a maroon cord held in his left hand, and a slender reed pen tucked visibly into his belt on the right side

ref_desc: Jayanaka is a mid-30s Kashmiri court poet with an oval light brown face, shoulder-length black hair under an off-white wool cap, cream angarkha, olive shawl-vest, maroon churidar, leather belt and sandals, carrying a rolled palm-leaf manuscript and reed pen in cream, maroon, olive, brown and black tones.
sheet_prompt: Full-body anime-style model sheet of Jayanaka: a mid-30s Kashmiri court poet with an oval light brown face, sharp nose, thoughtful dark eyes behind thin circular metal-framed spectacles, and a neat short beard and moustache, wearing straight shoulder-length black hair parted and tucked behind his ears under a soft off-white Kashmiri wool cap with a narrow maroon band at the base. He is dressed in a long-sleeved knee-length cream cotton angarkha with subtle woven stripes, side-tied with maroon cloth cords, layered with a sleeveless muted olive green wool shawl-vest draped over his shoulders and hanging to mid-thigh. His lower body has loose deep maroon churidar-style trousers gathered at the ankles, simple brown leather sandals, and a narrow dark brown leather belt carrying a small cloth pouch and a tiny copper tilak box. His signature props are a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a maroon cord in his left hand and a slender reed pen tucked visibly into his belt on the right, and his expression is calm, observant and slightly intense. Show him front, side, and back to clearly display the face, hair, cap, layered angarkha and shawl-vest, trousers, belt, sandals, and his manuscript and reed pen, using a palette dominated by cream, maroon, olive green, brown, and black.
